title: Understanding Japan: A Cultural History
description:
S01 E04 — Aspects of the Japanese Language
A complex writing system; how spoken Japanese reflects a long-standing concern with order, hierarchy and consensus; social context is important when speaking Japanese; the linguistic consequences of adopting Chinese characters in Japanese writing.

title: Understanding Japan: A Cultural History
description:
S01 E05 — Early Japanese Buddhism
Professor Ravina explains why Buddhism is so appealing in ancient Japan; three key observations about the religion's earliest form; the two main strands of Japanese Buddhism; the more esoteric tradition of Shingon; the more accessible Pure Land.

title: Understanding Japan: A Cultural History
description:
S01 E06 — Heian Court Culture
Japan's first period of isolation; the rise of the Heian court, ancient Japan's cultured and exclusive aristocracy; the powerful Fujiwara family; how the novel "The Tale of Genji" reveals the court's penchant for scandal and intrigue.

title: Understanding Japan: A Cultural History
description:
S01 E07 — The Rise of the Samurai
From the court in Kyoto to the countryside, where political infighting leads to the rise of Japan's first shogunate; the emergence of the samurai; the rise of warrior culture through the lines of "The Tale of the Heike", an epic ballad.

title: Understanding Japan: A Cultural History
description:
S01 E08 — Pure Land Buddhism and Zen Buddhism
The decline of the court and the rise of the warrior class shape the evolution of Buddhist aesthetic, spiritual and philosophical concepts; the massive growth of Pure Land Buddhism, the dominant form in Japan today; the main schools of Zen Buddhism.

title: Food: A Cultural Culinary History
description:
S01 E01 — Hunting, Gathering, and Stone Age Cooking
Food as a major catalyst in human history; what food choices reveal about one's values and ambitions; studying food culture in prehistoric times; a wide-ranging diet; the ways in which how human ancestors ate directly drove evolution.

title: Food: A Cultural Culinary History
description:
S01 E02 — What Early Agriculturalists Ate
The transition to agriculture; exploring the factors surrounding the rise of agriculture; how plants and animals were domesticated; why agriculture directly led to civilization; how the menu of foods favored by agricultural societies came about.

title: Food: A Cultural Culinary History
description:
S01 E03 — Egypt and the Gift of the Nile
Ancient Egypt's prosperity and advantages; a sophisticated food tradition and the first elite cuisine; the archeological evidence of Egypt's food customs; the religious significance of foodstuffs and animals; the components of Egyptian cuisine.

title: Food: A Cultural Culinary History
description:
S01 E04 — Ancient Judea - From Eden to Kosher Laws
Why practices regarding food were integral to the lives of the ancient Hebrews; exploring prescriptions regarding food in Genesis; considering that the Fall was an act of eating; Hebrew rituals and the meaning of sacrifice; complex food prohibitions.

title: Food: A Cultural Culinary History
description:
S01 E05 — Classical Greece - Wine, Olive Oil, and Trade
How the ancient Greeks' need for arable land led to their imperial and mercantile systems; what can be learned about ancient Greek food culture; the role of food in rituals; classical Greek diet components that later influenced the rest of the world.

title: Food: A Cultural Culinary History
description:
S01 E06 — The Alexandrian Exchange and the Four Humors
Alexander's conquests herald an era where previously unconnected cultures mix; tracing the diffusion of foodstuffs over trade networks in the Hellenistic period; studying early dietary regimens based on Galen's famous theory of the body's humors.

title: Food: A Cultural Culinary History
description:
S01 E07 — Ancient India - Sacred Cows and Ayurveda
Ancient India's culinary traditions carry a wide influence; learning about the culture of the Aryans, whose religion prefigures Hinduism; food customs relating to caste and the traditions of vegetarianism in Hinduism, Jainism, and Buddhism.

title: Food: A Cultural Culinary History
description:
S01 E08 — Yin and Yang of Classical Chinese Cuisine
Chinese culture produces what is arguably the most complex and varied culinary tradition on Earth; tracing the rise of civilization in China from the Hsia to the Han dynasty; the social and technological factors underlying China's food traditions.

title: Understanding Japan: A Cultural History
description:
S01 E01 — Japan: A Globally Engaged Island Nation
Japanese culture is shaped by powerful cycles of globalization and isolation; the earliest human habitation of Japan; the origins of its rich culture; the perfect starting points for dispelling common Western misconceptions about this island nation.

title: Understanding Japan: A Cultural History
description:
S01 E02 — Understanding Japan Through Ancient Myths
An introduction to ancient Japanese myths, collectively known as Shinto; the oldest written compilation of Japanese oral tradition, the Kojiki; stories about gods and heroes; the origins of the universe, the Rock Cave of Heaven and rival clans.

title: Understanding Japan: A Cultural History
description:
S01 E03 — The Emergence of the Ritsuryo State
In the late 500s, Japan begins a project of state building that evolves into the emperor-led Ritsuryo state; the state's laws and accomplishments; how this political centralization is inspired by the emergence of powerful states in China and Korea.

title: The Black Death: The World's Most Devastating Plague
description:
S01 E01 — Europe on the Brink of the Black Death
Contemplating the enormity of the Black Death's impact on the medieval world; taking account of the state of medieval society on the eve of the plague; investigating the religious, economic, and political structures of mid-14th-century Europe.

title: The Black Death: The World's Most Devastating Plague
description:
S01 E02 — The Epidemiology of Plague
Exploring the medical understanding of the plague; the sixth-century Plague of Justinian; the Black Death of the 1300s; the 19th-century Third Pandemic; examining the three predominant varieties of plague and their symptomatologies.

title: The Black Death: The World's Most Devastating Plague
description:
S01 E03 — Did Plague Really Cause the Black Death?
Reassessing the causes of the Black Death; questioning how it spread through medieval Europe with astonishing speed and virulence; investigating additional factors that may have contributed to the devastation, such as other diseases and bacteria.

title: The Black Death: The World's Most Devastating Plague
description:
S01 E04 — The Black Death's Ports of Entry
Examining the plague's first sustained appearance in Europe; the Mongol siege that preceded the outbreak; how the plague moved west with escaping sailors; following the spread of the plague to Constantinople, Italy, France and England.

title: The Great Revolutions of Modern History
description:
S01 E01 — Who Makes a Revolution?
Examining how revolutions arise from societal forces, and how they are seldom organized by the most downtrodden and repressed groups in a society.

title: The Great Revolutions of Modern History
description:
S01 E02 — Nationalism as Revolutionary Ideology
Exploring how social progress, literacy and the evolution of new cultural bonds led to revolutions in France, Italy and elsewhere.

title: The Great Revolutions of Modern History
description:
S01 E03 — Mexico's Revolution of Bullets and Myths
The Mexican Revolution is confounding for its many characters, as well as the twists and turns the revolution took.

title: The Great Revolutions of Modern History
description:
S01 E04 — The Man Who Lost the Russian Revolution
Exploring the Russian Revolution of 1917 and how it began with the promise of overthrowing the Romanov autocracy and ended with totalitarianism.

title: The Great Revolutions of Modern History
description:
S01 E05 — Totalitarianism and Counterrevolution
A look at what led to the rise of totalitarianism, and what it is like to live in such a state.

title: The Great Revolutions of Modern History
description:
S01 E06 — The US Civil Rights Revolution
Tracing the arc of African American history as it moved toward social equality and social justice.

title: Machiavelli in Context
description:
S01 E01 — Who Is Machiavelli? Why Does He Matter?
The course opens by placing Machiavelli in the context of the history of Western political thought, addressing the debate over the real Machiavelli, and examining his role as perhaps the first modern thinker.

title: Machiavelli in Context
description:
S01 E02 — Machiavelli's Florence
What sort of place Florence is in the period one calls the Renaissance; the lecture introduces an independent entity constantly working to gain an advantage over its Italian neighbors, dealing with the great European monarchies.

title: Machiavelli in Context
description:
S01 E03 — Classical Thought in Renaissance Florence
The Renaissance can best be understood as an educational movement that approaches and finds value in the classics in new ways; this lecture introduces the principal tenets of Renaissance Humanist thought and practice.

title: Machiavelli in Context
description:
S01 E04 — The Life of Niccolò Machiavelli
The republican interlude (1494–1512) that interrupts the Medici domination; Machiavelli leads an active life as a part of Florence's government; his most important writings come in the years after the Medici family re-establishes its rulership.

title: Machiavelli in Context
description:
S01 E05 — Why Did Machiavelli Write The Prince?
In studying Machiavelli's letters and "The Prince" itself, one learns the circumstances in which he produces his most famous work, and the degree to which his ideas, though owing much to classical thought, are quite original.

title: Machiavelli in Context
description:
S01 E06 — The Prince, 1-5-Republics Old and New
The lecture begins the in-depth exploration of "The Prince"; the view that it is an attempt to win the favor of the Medici; Machiavelli's first extended use of an example from classical antiquity to illuminate his discussion.

title: America's Founding Fathers
description:
S01 E01 — George Washington's Doubts
Explaining the importance of getting a well-rounded understanding of the Founders; Professor Guelzo explores Washington's fears about post-Revolutionary America; Washington's concerns about how people could administer their own affairs.

title: America's Founding Fathers
description:
S01 E02 — Thomas Mifflin's Congress
Before the ratification of the Constitution, there are presidents of the Congress created by the Articles of Confederation; the failures of one president, Thomas Mifflin, offer a window into the problems facing the United States of America in 1783.

title: America's Founding Fathers
description:
S01 E03 — Robert Morris's Money
Money issues abound in the new United States; why the abundance of land is a problem; what compels states to print their own paper money; how Robert Morris attempts to restore the links between commerce, agriculture and government finances.

title: America's Founding Fathers
description:
S01 E04 — Benjamin Franklin's Leather Apron
Exploring the many roles Benjamin Franklin plays in the formative years of the republic; this includes his part as an independent printer, a public "gentleman", a nobleman of nature and a tradesman cynical of the wealthy and powerful.

title: American Military History: From Colonials to Counterinsurgents
description:
S01 E01 — America: Forged in War
Exploring The French and Indian War of the mid-1700s, which is one of the formative conflicts in American military history; focusing on the experiences of Lt. Col. George Washington, a young colonial officer fighting for the British.

title: American Military History: From Colonials to Counterinsurgents
description:
S01 E02 — George Washington Takes Command
When the colonies begin their struggle for independence, they choose George Washington to lead the army; Washington's defense of Boston; his defeat trying to hold New York City; contrasting British and American objectives in the Revolutionary War.

title: American Military History: From Colonials to Counterinsurgents
description:
S01 E03 — Redcoats Fall to the Continental Army
Washington's army is in dire straits; his command is in question; he revives his reputation with the famous crossing of the Delaware River; the next four years of the American Revolution, which see Britain's strategic advantage deteriorate.

title: American Military History: From Colonials to Counterinsurgents
description:
S01 E04 — Andrew Jackson and the War of 1812
Why the United States chooses to fight Britain in the War of 1812; America's grievances and ambitions, which include the conquest of Canada; the poor strategy, command and training that lead to a strategic stalemate; the exception is Andrew Jackson.

title: American Military History: From Colonials to Counterinsurgents
description:
S01 E05 — The Mexican-American War of 1846-1848
The continental U.S. reaches its present span due to the Mexican-American War; the strategies and tactics of generals Zachary Taylor and Winfield Scott; what disciplined and bold maneuvers conducted by a professional army can accomplish.

title: American Military History: From Colonials to Counterinsurgents
description:
S01 E06 — Opening Volleys of the Civil War: 1861-1862
The Civil War sets the pattern for warfare in the 20th and 21st centuries; the political events leading up to the war; the strategy devised by Winfield Scott; the chaotic First Battle of Bull Run; developments in the western theater.

title: The US Constitution through History
description:
S01 E01 — America's Founding Ideas
Start the course on the U.S. Constitution by learning about the English culture that inspired American law and the conflict with England that caused the revolution.

title: The US Constitution through History
description:
S01 E02 — Failures of Early American Governments
Consider where the Articles of Confederation came from.

title: The US Constitution through History
description:
S01 E03 — Dilemmas of the Constitutional Convention
Witness the heated discussions surrounding the establishment of a new form of national governance.

title: The US Constitution through History
description:
S01 E04 — The Ratification of the Constitution
Reach back to the end of the eighteenth century and explore the attitudes of the various states towards the establishment of a unified federal government.

title: The US Constitution through History
description:
S01 E05 — The Bill of Rights as a Concession
Exploring the origins of the first ten amendments to the U.S. Constitution.

title: The US Constitution through History
description:
S01 E06 — The Rise of Federal Power: Hamilton's Bank
The central bank plays a critical role in determining the economic trajectory of a nation.

S01 E03 — Classical Thought in Renaissance Florence
The Renaissance can best be understood as an educational movement that approaches and finds value in the classics in new ways; this lecture introduces the principal tenets of Renaissance Humanist thought and practice.

title: Machiavelli in Context
description:
S01 E04 — The Life of Niccolò Machiavelli
The republican interlude (1494–1512) that interrupts the Medici domination; Machiavelli leads an active life as a part of Florence's government; his most important writings come in the years after the Medici family re-establishes its rulership.

title: Machiavelli in Context
description:
S01 E05 — Why Did Machiavelli Write The Prince?
In studying Machiavelli's letters and "The Prince" itself, one learns the circumstances in which he produces his most famous work, and the degree to which his ideas, though owing much to classical thought, are quite original.

title: Machiavelli in Context
description:
S01 E06 — The Prince, 1-5-Republics Old and New
The lecture begins the in-depth exploration of "The Prince"; the view that it is an attempt to win the favor of the Medici; Machiavelli's first extended use of an example from classical antiquity to illuminate his discussion.

title: The Black Death: The World's Most Devastating Plague
description:
S01 E01 — Europe on the Brink of the Black Death
Contemplating the enormity of the Black Death's impact on the medieval world; taking account of the state of medieval society on the eve of the plague; investigating the religious, economic, and political structures of mid-14th-century Europe.

title: The Black Death: The World's Most Devastating Plague
description:
S01 E02 — The Epidemiology of Plague
Exploring the medical understanding of the plague; the sixth-century Plague of Justinian; the Black Death of the 1300s; the 19th-century Third Pandemic; examining the three predominant varieties of plague and their symptomatologies.

title: The Black Death: The World's Most Devastating Plague
description:
S01 E03 — Did Plague Really Cause the Black Death?
Reassessing the causes of the Black Death; questioning how it spread through medieval Europe with astonishing speed and virulence; investigating additional factors that may have contributed to the devastation, such as other diseases and bacteria.

title: The Black Death: The World's Most Devastating Plague
description:
S01 E04 — The Black Death's Ports of Entry
Examining the plague's first sustained appearance in Europe; the Mongol siege that preceded the outbreak; how the plague moved west with escaping sailors; following the spread of the plague to Constantinople, Italy, France and England.

title: The Great Revolutions of Modern History
description:
S01 E01 — Who Makes a Revolution?
Examining how revolutions arise from societal forces, and how they are seldom organized by the most downtrodden and repressed groups in a society.

title: The Great Revolutions of Modern History
description:
S01 E02 — Nationalism as Revolutionary Ideology
Exploring how social progress, literacy and the evolution of new cultural bonds led to revolutions in France, Italy and elsewhere.

title: The Great Revolutions of Modern History
description:
S01 E03 — Mexico's Revolution of Bullets and Myths
The Mexican Revolution is confounding for its many characters, as well as the twists and turns the revolution took.

title: The Great Revolutions of Modern History
description:
S01 E04 — The Man Who Lost the Russian Revolution
Exploring the Russian Revolution of 1917 and how it began with the promise of overthrowing the Romanov autocracy and ended with totalitarianism.

title: The Great Revolutions of Modern History
description:
S01 E05 — Totalitarianism and Counterrevolution
A look at what led to the rise of totalitarianism, and what it is like to live in such a state.

title: The Great Revolutions of Modern History
description:
S01 E06 — The US Civil Rights Revolution
Tracing the arc of African American history as it moved toward social equality and social justice.

title: Machiavelli in Context
description:
S01 E01 — Who Is Machiavelli? Why Does He Matter?
The course opens by placing Machiavelli in the context of the history of Western political thought, addressing the debate over the real Machiavelli, and examining his role as perhaps the first modern thinker.

title: Machiavelli in Context
description:
S01 E02 — Machiavelli's Florence
What sort of place Florence is in the period one calls the Renaissance; the lecture introduces an independent entity constantly working to gain an advantage over its Italian neighbors, dealing with the great European monarchies.

title: Machiavelli in Context
description:
S01 E03 — Classical Thought in Renaissance Florence
The Renaissance can best be understood as an educational movement that approaches and finds value in the classics in new ways; this lecture introduces the principal tenets of Renaissance Humanist thought and practice.

title: A History of India
description:
S01 E01 — Earliest History of the Indian Subcontinent
Beginning one's study millions of years ago; plate tectonics shape the subcontinent's mountains, plateaus and river systems; these affect the region's aspects; reviewing South Asia's four macro-regions; how geography guides the course of life.

title: A History of India
description:
S01 E02 — Migration and the Adivasi
Three main cultures inhabit the ancient Indian subcontinent; studying the Adivasi, who once comprise the entirety of South Asia's population; how genetic and linguistic analysis shows the Adivasi of 30,000 years ago; their status in India today.

title: A History of India
description:
S01 E03 — Indus Valley Civilization
Turning to the urban people of the Indus Valley; many mysteries abound regarding this long-lost Bronze Age civilization; exploring excavated cities; examining art and artifacts; what people know about this society; what may have happened to them.

title: A History of India
description:
S01 E04 — Indo-European Vedic Culture
Exploring the ancient foundations of Hinduism, which emerge from people who identify themselves with the Vedas; studying these poems and hymns; the civilization's culture and cosmology; the origins and development of the Indo-European language.

title: A History of India
description:
S01 E05 — Caste: Varna and Jati
The Vedic caste system is one of the most well-known and misunderstood aspects of Hindu society; the ancient Vedic social order; how it structures society; how numerous inherited social groups relate to occupation; a diverse and complex society.

title: Early Humans: Ice, Stone, and Survival
description:
S01 E01 — What Does It Mean to Be Human?
Exploring human development and the considering questions about early life.

title: Early Humans: Ice, Stone, and Survival
description:
S01 E02 — Stones and Bones: The First Fossil Families
Homo habilis, the earliest known species of the genus.

title: Early Humans: Ice, Stone, and Survival
description:
S01 E03 — Bio-Cultural Adaptation andHomo erectus
Meeting Homo erectus, the first of the genus to walk completely upright.

title: Early Humans: Ice, Stone, and Survival
description:
S01 E04 — HowHomo sapiensLeft Africa
Exploring the roles of gene flow and the exchanges of artifacts, ideas and social structure.

title: Early Humans: Ice, Stone, and Survival
description:
S01 E05 — X-Woman! Meet Our Ancient Relatives
Discovering the complexity of early human history by meeting Denny, a female specimen.

title: Early Humans: Ice, Stone, and Survival
description:
S01 E06 — Did the Neanderthals Really Go Extinct?
Exploring the culture-rich lives of the Neanderthals, who existed for more than 300,000 years across a vast geographic space.

title: The Big History of Civilizations
description:
S01 E01 — A Tale of Two Ancient Cities
Jericho and Anau are two of the world's oldest cities; their stories have much to say about the scope of human history; what makes these cities successful; how they differ from each other; introducing the concept and key themes of Big History.

title: The Big History of Civilizations
description:
S01 E02 — The Rise of Humanity
Tracing the origins of the human species from the emergence of proto-humans to the rise of Homo sapiens, Professor Benjamin offers perspectives to show what makes the human species unique and why it has been able to flourish.

title: The Big History of Civilizations
description:
S01 E03 — Foraging in the Old Stone Age
The Paleolithic Era is the longest time in human history; understanding this period is crucial for comprehending the human history that follows, including how family dynamics, migration patterns, climate change and more affect life in this era.

title: The Big History of Civilizations
description:
S01 E04 — Origins of Agriculture
Debating why and how humanity transitions from foraging to agriculture; delving into the agricultural revolution; how some combination of climate change, population growth and human ingenuity leads to a revolution in human history.

title: The Big History of Civilizations
description:
S01 E05 — Power, Cities, and States
The next major transition in human history is the rise of cities; introducing life in the early farm communities; Professor Benjamin investigates the origins of power; its relationship to the state; the abiding features of the world's early cities.
